title: Effects of whole-body electromyostimulation training on glycaemia and physical performance in adults with double diabetes
summary: The present randomized and controlled trial at two study centres investigates the effect of whole-body electromyostimulation training (WB-EMS) on glucose metabolism and physical performance in adults with type 1 diabetes (T1DM) associated with features of metabolic syndrome and type II diabetes (T2DM) (= double diabetes: DD).  A total of 48 adults with DD will  be randomly allocated to a WB-EMS (n=24) and a non-training control group (n=24).  The duration of the training intervention will be 4 months, the training duration 1.5x 20 min per week (...i.e. 3 training sessions in 2 weeks). The intervention effect will be determined by comparing the changes in the time in which the glucose concentration is between 70-180 mg/dL (so-called Time in Range: TIR) in the WB-EMS versus non-training control group. In addition, various other parameters of glucose metabolism, cardiometabolic risk factors, physical fitness, attractiveness and safety of the WB-EMS programme are considered as secondary outcomes. The statistical analysis includes an intention to treat analysis with multiple imputation using appropriate statistical methods to address our study endpoints, and is performed by a qualified external statistician, as is the randomization procedure.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Legally competent men and women with clinically manifest T1DM
At least one additional criterion of metabolic syndrome according to the International Diabetes Federation, i.e.   
     Abdominal circumference ≥94 cm (men) or ≥80 cm (women)
     Triglyceride values ≥150 mg/dl or treatment already initiated 
     HDL cholesterol <40 mg/dl (men) <50 mg/dl (women) or therapy 
      High blood pressure (systolic ≥130, diastolic ≤85 mmHg) or therapy 
Overweight (BMI ≥25.0 kg/m2)
HbA1c >6.5%
Exclusion criteria:
Cardiovascular diseases, in particular high-grade cardiac arrhythmia / atrial fibrillation / pacemaker or heart failure > NYHA1 
High-grade (drug-treated) obstructive and restrictive lung disease (asthma / COPD / PHT) 
epilepsy 
Severe circulatory disordersGFR<60; diabetic nephropathy  
Regular (≥ 1TE/week) strength training in the last 8 weeks
Contraindications for the use of MRI
Absolute contraindications for WB-EMS
Anticipated absence ≥ 3 weeks during the intervention period
